messages.subject: new ggplot2 web application
parts:
http://yeroon.net/ggplot2 shows a first version of a new web
application for exploratory graphical analysis. It attempts to
implement the layered graphics from ggplot2 in a user-friendly way.
This two-minute demo video demonstrates a quick how-to:
http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_haIgb4nFFY&hd=1. Data can be uploaded
in .csv, spss (.sav) or tab delimited format, but make sure it
includes headers (column names).

We hope that you will give it a try. The tool is still in early
production. If you encounter any problems, unclarities, or have ideas
for improvement, please do send some feedback; we appreciate it.

Jeroen

messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: new ggplot2 web application
parts:
Very slick. This is fantastic work. It feels smooth and easy. The
enumeration of the options through the menu system give the user a
good idea of what options are available, whereas you need to go to the
docs in the command line. I know how hard it is to make a nice
interface, and yours is quite elegant.

Two minor points:
1. When editing the layer options, one has to navigate through 4
levels of contextual menus. If I need to change a couple options for a
single layer (as you did in your demo) I need to travel through this
deep structure multiple times.

2. When I right click on the x/y labels or the legend I expected to be
able to edit them.

One major point:
1. I know everyone has their own opinions about how they like to
interface with their software, but the biggest limitation for me is
that this is locked up in a web app. I (and everyone I know) do all my
data manipulation and analysis on a local machine. To then have to
write it out to a local file and load it to the web (unencrypted) is
simply not going to happen for me. Perhaps an SPSS / non-R user would
be more inclined to do so because of limitations in SPSS.


Cheers,
Ian

p.s. How have we not met? I think I'm down the hall from you (in the
first year PhD office). Drop me a line...

messages.author: 3ea57457192f4f3b
messages.subject: Re: new ggplot2 web application
parts:
Some updates to the http://yeroon.net/ggplot2 web application:

- SYNTAX MODE: webapp now includes a super secret tiny arrow in the
center-bottom of the page, that opens a syntax window. This is a
feature some people requested. It should interactively show you the
code used to plot the current graph. Please let me know your
experiences, and if it generates sensible code.

- Now works in IE: there was some bug that prevented the application
from properly displaying in Internet Explorer. It should be fixed now.
Supported browsers are Internet Explorer 6+, FireFox 1.5+ (PC, Mac),
Safari 3+, and Chrome, however a recent browser is more than highly
recommended. For best performance use Chrome 3 or Safari 4.

Furthermore, many people seem to have problems uploading their data.
To avoid any confusion: if the filename ends with .csv, the data is
imported using read.csv("filename.csv",header=T); if it ends
with .sav, it uses read.spss("filename.sav"), and in all other cases
it uses read.table("filename.txt", header=T). I'm working on something
better. Any suggestions on this part are welcome too.

Jeroen
